lastCompletedStory.title: Durable behavioral test that the shipped template ignores every cam runtime artifact

nextStoryContext: US-003 added test/templates-gitignore-runtime-artifacts.test.ts, modeled on test/templates-gitignore-dotenv.test.ts (CAM-499) but with a STRICT isIgnored helper (`if (r.exitCode > 1) throw`, never folding a fatal error into 'not ignored'). It drives real `git check-ignore` against materializeTemplates's output on both the verbatim-write and mergeGitignore paths, asserting all 16 US-001+US-002 runtime artifacts (3 from US-001: sidecar-liveness-watcher log/pid, merge-watch state; 13 from US-002: the DIVERGE lines the parity script found on main) are ignored, plus two negative controls in both blanket directions (.claude/agents/subagent-planner.md against a blanket .claude/*, scripts/cam/patterns.md against a blanket scripts/cam/*) -- both controls ship as real template content so no synthesis was needed, they exist on disk immediately after materializeTemplates runs. Falsifiability swept in 3 mutations, each via bun run embed-vendor (never mutating templates/.gitignore alone, per GOTCHA 3): (1) deleting the .claude/.cam-gate.json rule -> RED on both paths at the artifact-coverage assertion; (2) substituting the whole .claude/... block with a blanket .claude/* -> RED at the first negative control only; (3) substituting the scripts/cam/*.json|txt rules with a blanket scripts/cam/* -> RED at the second negative control only, while the first stayed green (confirmed via expect() call count: 42 = full-green count vs 38 under mutation 2), proving the two controls are independently scoped. All 3 mutations fully reverted (git status --short + embed-vendor:check clean) before committing. patterns.md bullet appended under CAM-502 tag with the exact assertion lines observed failing. No new stories remain unassigned to me from this PRD's spawn context; check prd.json for the next pending US-XXX.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed exit codes: 0 = at least one path ignored, 1 = none ignored, 128 = fatal error. The test's isIgnored helper's `if (r.exitCode > 1) throw` matches exactly: any code above 1 is treated as an error, never as a verdict.
